full_judgment: 18. The defendant-appellants' claim that their landlord Hari Prasad Das's father Baroda Prasad Das took settlement from BinoyendraAich in 1940 and, as such, it cannot be said that the origin of their tenancy for residential purpose was unknown. But, in fact, they could not produce any paper in support of their claim. Further, they do not claim to have constructed any permanent structure on the land to the knowledge of Baroda Prasad Das, from whom they took the settlement. On the other hand, they claim that Baroda Prasad Das erected twelve huts in plot No. 947 and used to reside in some huts with his family and used to possess the other huts through monthly tenants. Upon these facts no substantial findings can be made out that any pucca building on the land was built to the knowledge of the landlord to justify the presumption of permanency of tenancy. The defendant-appellants also claim that the Municipal holding was also created in his father's name and he has been paying municipal taxes regularly. Admittedly, all the courts have found them in possession but they could not produce any patta kabuliyat in support of the alleged settlement in favour of Baroda Prasad Das from Binoyendra Aich in the year 1940. Three typed receipts have been marked as exhibit I series in Title Suit No. 133 of 1981 to prove the payment of ground taxes to Binayendra Aich. In these receipts it is mentioned that Rs. 60.00 was received by Binayendra Aich in respect of ground tax and municipal holding Nos. 185, 186 and 152(a) of Bazrapur Mohalla of Comilla Town. All the courts below held that from these receipts it could not be said that Baroda Prasad took settlement of the said land from Binayendra Aich. We do not also find any reason to disagree with them. Thus the defendant appellants failed to establish uniform payment of rent raising difficulties in the way of presumption of permanency of tenancy.
